bug_semantics: The awx CLI import command parses attacker-supplied YAML from client.stdin with awxkit.yaml_file.Loader. Loader registers !include and !import, and extractFile joins the directive value to the input stream's directory (which is empty for <stdin>), expands the result with glob.glob, converts matches to absolute paths, and opens and recursively parses them without rejecting absolute paths, '..' traversal, or symlink escapes. A user who imports a malicious YAML document can therefore disclose arbitrary locally readable YAML-formatted files.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable Loader and extractFile implementation first enters ansible/awx public history in 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507, but that commit is a 101-file, 10,479-line component import titled 'import awxkit', and PR #4451 is titled 'open source awxkit'. It is an aggregate publication/migration boundary, not the smallest commit that originally wrote the flawed path-resolution mechanism. The pre-import awxkit/towerkit commit lineage needed to identify that smallest BIC is not present in the validated clone or reconstructable from the public PR members.
ai_marker: unavailable because the true smallest BIC commit object is outside the accessible public history. The non-BIC public import object 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507 was checked only as a boundary: author and committer are Ryan Petrello <rpetrell@redhat.com>; its trailers are six named human Co-authored-by entries and contain no AI/Generated-with marker. Those boundary-object facts are not used to attribute the unavailable BIC.
evidence: GitHub advisory https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-G29C-RGQ6-GXGJ describes CVE-2026-52902/GHSA-g29c-rgq6-gxgj as arbitrary local YAML-file disclosure through !include during 'awx --conf.format yaml import', marks awxkit <=24.6.1 vulnerable, and gives no first patched version. In awxkit/awxkit/cli/resource.py:81-103, Import.handle calls yaml.load(client.stdin, Loader=yaml_file.Loader). In awxkit/awxkit/yaml_file.py, vulnerable release 24.6.1 sets _root=os.path.split(stream.name)[0], registers !include/!import, then extractFile performs os.path.join, glob.glob, os.path.abspath, open, and yaml.load with no containment check. `git log --all -S"Loader.add_constructor('!include'" -- awxkit/awxkit/yaml_file.py` returns only 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507 (2019-08-08, 'import awxkit'). `git show --format=raw --stat --summary 9616...` shows one parent 9b836abf1fc36c703c26683fd7bf1343254bff91 and 101 new awxkit files/10,479 insertions; https://github.com/ansible/awx/pull/4451 calls it 'open source awxkit', and its public member list contains only the aggregate import 9616... and later CI cleanup adaa4148c69592e504a232a54cd6b767d32628d7, so no original vulnerable-line member can be decomposed. `git diff-tree --name-status 9b836... 9616... -- awxkit/awxkit/yaml_file.py` reports A, directly proving the file is absent from the aggregate import's parent tree; this proves the public migration boundary, not parent absence for an unknown original BIC. `git tag --contains 9616...` includes 7.0.0 through 24.6.1; tag 24.6.1 resolves to 94e5795dfc37b95c576d61f3e3b4e936c021548c and its yaml_file.py retains the unsafe code. Fix https://github.com/ansible/awx/commit/405c56e2bcaee1965a6f57520623cfa47612c9e2.patch adds absolute-path, normalized containment, realpath/symlink, and stdin rejection checks plus regression tests; its immediate parent 413dfed16c6636961005cbb164186b5bd95872d9 still has the unsafe implementation. `git tag --contains 405c56...` is empty, consistent with the advisory's null patched version.
reasoning: The advisory's attack path is causal: import parses untrusted YAML locally; !include reaches extractFile; an absolute path discards _root in os.path.join and a relative ../ path escapes it; glob resolves matches; open/yaml.load discloses readable YAML content before the imported assets are sent to AWX. Commit 405c56e2bcaee1965a6f57520623cfa47612c9e2 directly closes every relevant escape class and is therefore both the lifecycle fix and direct fix. History and tags establish that the unsafe component was publicly present from the 2019 awxkit import through the last affected 24.6.1 release, while the fix remains untagged. However, protocol forbids treating a move or aggregate import as the BIC. The only public first-hit commit is demonstrably a wholesale open-sourcing import, and neither its parent nor PR members preserve the earlier component history. Consequently the true smallest commit, its immediate parent, and its commit-object AI signals cannot be inspected. The boundary commit's human-only object cannot support NOT_AI for code it merely aggregated, so the correct verdict is BLOCKED rather than a fabricated closed attribution.
remaining_gap: The original pre-open-source awxkit/towerkit commit history is unavailable: specifically, the commit that first wrote the unsanitized !include path-resolution lines, that commit's immediate parent tree, and that BIC commit object's author/committer/trailers. Without that lineage, the aggregate 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507 cannot be decomposed to a protocol-valid BIC or assigned an AI verdict. Separately, no released patched awxkit version exists as of the audited history; the direct fix is present only in untagged commit 405c56e2bcaee1965a6f57520623cfa47612c9e2.
